record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: For a group G and a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C that is closed under complex conjugation, let R_FG be the *-regular closure of FG inside the algebra U(G) of affiliated operators. Is the canonical map colim_{H ⊆ G, |H| < ∞} K_0(FH) → K_0(FG) → K_0(R_FG) always surjective?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9 (Algebraic Atiyah Conjecture). Let G be a group and let F be a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C, which is closed under complex conjugation. Let RF G be the ∗-regular closure of F G in U(G). We say that G satisfies the Algebraic Atiyah Conjecture with coefficients in F if the composite of the canonical maps colimH⊆G,|H|<∞ K0(F H) → K0(F G) → K0(RF G) is surjective.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete group and let $F$ be a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ with $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq F \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ that is closed under complex conjugation. Denote by $\mathcal{N}(G)$ the group von Neumann algebra of $G$ and by $\mathcal{U}(G)$ the algebra of operators affiliated to $\mathcal{N}(G)$. The group ring $FG$ embeds into $\mathcal{U}(G)$. A subring $R \subseteq \mathcal{U}(G)$ is called $*$-regular if it is closed under the involution $*$ inherited from $\mathcal{U}(G)$ and is von Neumann regular (i.e., for every $r \in R$ there exists $s \in R$ with $rsr = r$). The $*$-regular closure $\mathcal{R}_{FG}$ of $FG$ in $\mathcal{U}(G)$ is the smallest $*$-regular subring of $\mathcal{U}(G)$ containing $FG$.

For each finite subgroup $H \leq G$, the inclusion $FH \hookrightarrow FG$ induces a map on the Grothendieck groups of finitely generated projective modules $K_0(FH) \to K_0(FG)$, and these assemble into a map $\mathrm{colim}_{H \leq G,\, |H|<\infty} K_0(FH) \to K_0(FG)$. Composing with the map $K_0(FG) \to K_0(\mathcal{R}_{FG})$ induced by the inclusion $FG \hookrightarrow \mathcal{R}_{FG}$ yields a canonical homomorphism
$$\Phi_{G,F}\colon \mathrm{colim}_{H \leq G,\, |H| < \infty} K_0(FH) \longrightarrow K_0(\mathcal{R}_{FG}).$$

Determine whether $\Phi_{G,F}$ is surjective for every group $G$ and every such field $F$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Algebraic Atiyah Conjecture remains open in general. Recent work (2024–2025) on universal localizations and graphs of groups by Jaikin-Zapirain and collaborators establishes the surjectivity in new cases (e.g., graphs of groups with finite edge groups under bounded finite subgroup orders) but the conjecture for arbitrary $G$ and $F$ is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Universal localizations, Atiyah conjectures and graphs of groups
status_evidence.snippet: The algebraic and center-valued Atiyah conjectures over K are closed under the graph of groups construction as long as the edge groups are finite.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results extend the conjecture to graphs of groups with finite edge groups, indicating it is still being actively investigated rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Universal Localizations, Atiyah Conjectures and Graphs of Groups (GAFA 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: The algebraic Atiyah conjecture for G over K holds if the map ⊕ K_0(K[F]) → K_0(R_{K[G]}) is surjective.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated and proven only in specific cases (graph-of-groups constructions), confirming the general statement remains open.
